title: The King Grants Their Lives

Troubled by Ammon’s generosity and words, he asks why Ammon did not accompany them from Middoni. Aaron explains that the Spirit of the Lord called Ammon another way and that he went to Ishmael to teach Lamoni’s people.

title: The Lands and Their Borders
summary: The king sent a proclamation throughout his land. The account describes where the Lamanites and Nephites lived, the lands of Bountiful and Desolation, and the small neck of land. The Nephites inhabited Bountiful and used guards and armies to hem in the Lamanites on the south.

explicit_facts.text: The king sent a proclamation throughout his land, which was divided from Zarahemla by a narrow strip of wilderness.
Some Lamanites dwelt in tents in western wilderness and seashore areas.
Many Lamanites were by the eastern seashore, where the Nephites had driven them; the Nephites held northern lands extending to Bountiful.
Bountiful bordered Desolation, which extended into a land that had been peopled and destroyed.
Desolation was north of Bountiful; the wilderness contained wild animals, some of which had come from the north for food.
The line between Bountiful and Desolation was a day and a half’s journey for a Nephite from the east to the west sea; a small neck of land lay between the northern and southern lands.
The Nephites inhabited Bountiful from the east to the west sea and, with guards and armies, had hemmed in the Lamanites on the south.
The Lamanites could have possessions only in the land of Nephi and the surrounding wilderness; the Nephites sought to retain a country to which they could flee.
